content.text:
### Is the Session thread-safe? Is AsyncSession safe to share in concurrent tasks?

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_basics.html

The [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session') is a **mutable, stateful** object that represents a **single database transaction**. An instance of [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session') therefore **cannot be shared among concurrent threads or asyncio tasks without careful synchronization**. The [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session') is intended to be used in a **non-concurrent** fashion, that is, a particular instance of [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session') should be used in only one thread or task at a time.

When using the [`AsyncSession`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession 'sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession') object from SQLAlchemy’s [asyncio](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html) extension, this object is only a thin proxy on top of a [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session'), and the same rules apply; it is an **unsynchronized, mutable, stateful object**, so it is **not** safe to use a single instance of [`AsyncSession`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession 'sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession') in multiple asyncio tasks at once.

--------------------------------

### Session Basics

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_basics.html

The concurrency model for SQLAlchemy’s [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session') and [`AsyncSession`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession 'sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession') is therefore **Session per thread, AsyncSession per task**. An application that uses multiple threads, or multiple tasks in asyncio such as when using an API like `asyncio.gather()` would want to ensure that each thread has its own [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session'), each asyncio task has its own [`AsyncSession`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession 'sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession').

--------------------------------

### AsyncSession.is_active

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html

True if this Session is not in 'partial rollback' state. 'Partial rollback' state typically indicates that the flush process of the Session has failed, and that the Session.rollback() method must be emitted in order to fully roll back the transaction.

```APIDOC
## AsyncSession.is_active

### Description
True if this Session is not in 'partial rollback' state. 'Partial rollback' state typically indicates that the flush process of the Session has failed, and that the Session.rollback() method must be emitted in order to fully roll back the transaction.

### Type
bool

### Notes
- Proxied for the Session class on behalf of the AsyncSession class.
- Changed in version 1.4: The Session no longer begins a new transaction immediately, so this attribute will be False when the Session is first instantiated.
```

--------------------------------

### Session Basics

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_basics.html

When a failure occurs within a flush, in order to continue using that same [`Session`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session'), an explicit call to [`Session.rollback()`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session.rollback 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session.rollback') is required after a flush fails, even though the underlying transaction will have been rolled back already (even if the database driver is technically in driver-level autocommit mode). This is so that the overall nesting pattern of so-called “subtransactions” is consistently maintained. The FAQ section [“This Session’s transaction has been rolled back due to a previous exception during flush.” (or similar)](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/faq/sessions.html#faq-session-rollback) contains a more detailed description of this behavior.

See also

[“This Session’s transaction has been rolled back due to a previous exception during flush.” (or similar)](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/faq/sessions.html#faq-session-rollback) - further background on why [`Session.rollback()`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.Session.rollback 'sqlalchemy.orm.Session.rollback') must be called when a flush fails.

--------------------------------

### Synopsis - ORM

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html

Warning

A single instance of [`AsyncSession`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession 'sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession') is **not safe for use in multiple, concurrent tasks**. See the sections [Using AsyncSession with Concurrent Tasks](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#asyncio-concurrency) and [Is the Session thread-safe? Is AsyncSession safe to share in concurrent tasks?](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_basics.html#session-faq-threadsafe) for background.

arguments.query: SQLAlchemy 2.0 PostgreSQL ExcludeConstraint where gist btree_gist && overlap range

content.text:
### ExcludeConstraint.__init__

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/postgresql.html

Create an ExcludeConstraint object. The constraint is defined by a sequence of (column, operator) tuples, with optional where and ops parameters.

```APIDOC
## ExcludeConstraint.__init__

### Description
Create an ExcludeConstraint object. The constraint is normally embedded into the Table construct directly, or added later using append_constraint().

### Method
`__init__`

### Signature
```python
ExcludeConstraint(*elements: Tuple[_DDLColumnArgument, str], **kw: Any) -> None
```

### Parameters
- **\*elements** (Tuple[_DDLColumnArgument, str]) - Required - A sequence of two tuples of the form `(column, operator)` where "column" is either a Column object, a SQL expression element (e.g. `func.int8range(table.from, table.to)`), or the name of a column as string, and "operator" is a string containing the operator to use (e.g. "&&" or "=").
- **\*\*kw** (Any) - Optional - Additional keyword arguments. Supported keywords include:
  - **where** - SQL expression for a WHERE clause to apply to the constraint.
  - **ops** - Dictionary mapping column names to custom operator classes.
  - **name** - Name of the constraint.

### Example
```python
const = ExcludeConstraint(
    (Column("period"), "&&"),
    (Column("group"), "="),
    where=(Column("group") != "some group"),
    ops={"group": "my_operator_class"},
)
```

### Usage with Table
```python
some_table = Table(
    "some_table",
    metadata,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column("period", TSRANGE()),
    Column("group", String),
)

some_table.append_constraint(
    ExcludeConstraint(
        (some_table.c.period, "&&"),
        (some_table.c.group, "="),
        where=some_table.c.group != "some group",
        name="some_table_excl_const",
        ops={"group": "my_operator_class"},
    )
)
```

### Notes
The exclude constraint defined in this example requires the `btree_gist` extension, that can be created using the command `CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist;`.
```

--------------------------------

### Append ExcludeConstraint to a Table using append_constraint()

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/postgresql.html

Defines a Table with columns and then appends an ExcludeConstraint using append_constraint(). This example requires the btree_gist extension (CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist;).

```python
some_table = Table(
    "some_table",
    metadata,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column("period", TSRANGE()),
    Column("group", String),
)

some_table.append_constraint(
    ExcludeConstraint(
        (some_table.c.period, "&&"),
        (some_table.c.group, "="),
        where=some_table.c.group != "some group",
        name="some_table_excl_const",
        ops={"group": "my_operator_class"},
    )
)
```

--------------------------------

### ExcludeConstraint

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/postgresql.html

The ExcludeConstraint class represents a PostgreSQL exclusion constraint, which ensures that certain conditions are not met for any two rows. It is used in the __table_args__ of a declarative model.

```APIDOC
## ExcludeConstraint

### Description

A PostgreSQL exclusion constraint that ensures that if any two rows are compared on the specified columns or expressions using the specified operators, at least one of these operator comparisons will return false or null. It is typically used to prevent overlapping ranges or other conflicting data.

### Parameters

- **name** (string) - Optional - The in-database name of this constraint.
- **deferrable** (bool) - Optional - If set, emit DEFERRABLE or NOT DEFERRABLE when issuing DDL for this constraint.
- **initially** (string) - Optional - If set, emit INITIALLY <value> when issuing DDL for this constraint.
- **info** (dict) - Optional - Data dictionary populated into the SchemaItem.info attribute. Added in version 2.0.50.
- **using** (string) - Optional - If set, emit USING <index_method> when issuing DDL for this constraint. Defaults to 'gist'.
- **where** (SQL expression or string) - Optional - If set, emit WHERE <predicate> when issuing DDL for this constraint.
- **ops** (dict) - Optional - Dictionary defining operator classes for the elements; works like the postgresql_ops parameter of Index. Added in version 1.3.21.

### Example

```python
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import ExcludeConstraint, TSRANGE

class RoomBooking(Base):
    __tablename__ = "room_booking"

    room = Column(Integer(), primary_key=True)
    during = Column(TSRANGE())

    __table_args__ = (ExcludeConstraint(("room", "="), ("during", "&&")),)
```
```

--------------------------------

### Create ExcludeConstraint with columns, operators, where, and ops

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/postgresql.html

Constructs an ExcludeConstraint using Column objects, operators, a where clause, and custom operator class. The constraint can be added to a Table.

```python
const = ExcludeConstraint(
    (Column("period"), "&&"),
    (Column("group"), "="),
    where=(Column("group") != "some group"),
    ops={"group": "my_operator_class"},
)
```

--------------------------------

### Define ExcludeConstraint with TSRANGE for Room Booking

Source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/postgresql.html

Use ExcludeConstraint in __table_args__ to prevent overlapping time ranges for the same room. The constraint uses the && operator on the during column and the = operator on the room column.

```python
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import ExcludeConstraint, TSRANGE


class RoomBooking(Base):
    __tablename__ = "room_booking"

    room = Column(Integer(), primary_key=True)
    during = Column(TSRANGE())

    __table_args__ = (ExcludeConstraint(("room", "="), ("during", "&&")),)
```
